#tb 1940’s & today: Looking north at Myrtle Ave & St. Nicholas Ave in Ridgewood, Queens.
.
Whilst this spot has changed a bit over the years, it is still pleasant to see that many of the old buildings seen in the old photo are still standing today, albeit with a few alterations. One thing that certainly is no longer around, however, is the trolley and tracks seen turning onto Myrtle Avenue from St. Nicholas Avenue. The sign on the top of the trolley reads “Bushwick” so I’m inclined to believe the car belonged to the Bushwick Avenue Line which ran between Williamsburg and Ridgewood but I’m not exactly certain. If it is in fact the Bushwick Avenue Line, it ceased operations in 1947.

L'interno della basilica di San Paolo fuori le Mura, Roma. 

È una delle quattro basiliche papali di Roma, la seconda più grande dopo quella di San Pietro in Vaticano.
La basilica di San Paolo fuori le Mura presenta una pianta a croce latina; l'aula è divisa in cinque navate, separate da quattro file di 20 colonne monolitiche di granito di Montorfano.

Al centro del transetto della basilica, sotto l'arco trionfale, si trova il Ciborio, in stile gotico, di Arnolfo di Cambio che lo realizzò per volere dell'abate Bartolomeo nel 1285.

Alex Zablocki is an American Ceramic Artist whose work takes apart the ceramic vessel and re-animates its constituent parts, incorporating vestiges of utilitarian ceramics which slip along saturations of colored glaze.

A double Duchess special!

There’s two BR Maroon Coronations in the fleet, those are 46229 ‘Duchess of Hamilton’ and 46256 ‘Sir William Stanier F.R.S.’

Whilst on the outside they carry a lot of similarity, they also aptly represent the life span of the class, with ‘Duchess of Hamilton’ representing built in 1938 being the 10th of the class and ‘Sir William Stanier F.R.S.’ Being the 38th & penultimate locomotive built nearly a decade later in 1947 to a revised design that was designed to improve performance and lengthen the time needed between heavy overhauls. 

Both finished their working lives as seen here, with 46229’s streamlined casing being a distant memory and both wearing the London Midland Regions distinctive Maroon livery that 16 of the class were eventually given in their final years in homage to their LMS heritage.

An HO scale model of Conrail's Philadelphia Division Safety On Rails Theater car. 
This car was a staple at events in and around NJ in the 90s.  I remember as a kid seeing it at the Hoboken Terminal festival along with its companion N21 Operation Lifesaver caboose.  The car still exists today, painted and lettered TOYX 1775 for Operation Toy Train.  It currently resides at the Port Jervis Transportation History Center. 

The model is built from a #tangentscalemodels X58 kit with lots of little mods and details to match prototype photos.  The car was painted with @tru.colorpaint rich oxide brown, lightly weathered and decaled with a mix of Microscale, @cmrproducts_com, and custom printed decals I made myself.
